predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: the counties of Troyes, Reims-side Champagne and Langres borderland as Cliopatria draws them in 990

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the county, reunited with the royal domain by Philip IV's marriage to Joan I in 1284

successors.name: Royal domain of France
successors.text: Champagne and Brie in the royal domain

ledger.x: 1003: a block at Sens and Joigny joins the Champagne shape.
1022: Odo II of Blois takes Champagne.
1037: Stephen II inherits Troyes, Meaux and Vitry.
1055: the block at Sens leaves the Champagne shape.
1063: Theobald III of Blois reunites Blois and Champagne.
1089: Champagne is divided from Blois again.
1125: Theobald IV of Blois becomes Count of Champagne and Brie.
1284: Joan I marries Philip IV and Champagne joins the royal domain.

wars.name: Louis VII's war against Theobald II of Champagne
wars.outcome: The conflict 'lasted two years (1142-1144)'; Champagne was occupied by the royal army and Vitry-le-François captured.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Champagne
wars.outcome: It 'broke into open warfare in 1215' and was 'not resolved until after Theobald came of age in 1222', when he 'bought out their rights for a substantial monetary payment'.

wars.name: Baronial invasion of Champagne
wars.outcome: In 1229-1230 Henry II of Bar attacked from the east and Hugh IV of Burgundy from the south; Blanche of Castile intervened to stop the fighting.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages opened; Champagne's frontier with the Empire and the bishoprics of Reims, Auxerre and Langres is a ring of castles and homages (Henry the Liberal's nine border castles).
